overview.problemStatement: An organizer with only a rough idea must fill in a long create-event form, which is slow and often produces thin descriptions.
overview.proposedSolution: A Generate with AI dialog sends a free-text prompt to a Next.js route handler that calls the Cerebras SDK and returns a structured draft (title, description, category, suggested capacity, suggested ticket type) that fills the form for editing before save.
overview.targetAudience: Event organizers on the create-event page.
assumptions: retroactive: true - documented from the existing implementation during brownfield onboarding; it is not a forward-looking product decision.
AI output is a draft only; nothing is persisted until the organizer submits the normal create-event form.
The Cerebras key lives in the server environment as CEREBRAS_API_KEY.
@google/generative-ai is installed but is not used by this flow.
outOfScope: Generating images, prices, venues, or dates.

userStories.title: Generate event details from a prompt
userStories.want: to describe my idea and get a filled draft
userStories.benefit: I can start from something concrete

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the dialog is open, when I submit a non-empty prompt, a loading state shows, the request goes to POST /api/generate-event, and the returned title, description, category, suggested capacity, and suggested ticket type fill the form.

userStories.title: Rely on a stable server contract
userStories.want: a defined request and response shape
userStories.benefit: the form can map the result deterministically

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a body without a prompt, the endpoint responds 400 with an error; given a valid prompt, it responds with JSON containing title, description, category, suggestedCapacity, and suggestedTicketType.

userStories.title: Keep the provider key server-side
userStories.want: the provider key kept on the server
userStories.benefit: it cannot be scraped from the browser

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the route runs, it reads CEREBRAS_API_KEY from the server environment, and no provider key appears in client bundles or responses; a missing key produces a clear server error.

userStories.title: Review before saving
userStories.benefit: the AI cannot publish an inaccurate event on its own

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given generated values, they only populate form fields, and the event is created only when I submit the validated form, with all fields still editable.

userStories.title: Fail safely
userStories.want: a failed generation to be visible
userStories.benefit: I am not left with a silently broken form

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a network or JSON parsing failure, an error toast is shown, the dialog stays open, and the form is not populated.

functionalRequirements.text: The create-event page MUST offer a prompt dialog that requests generated event data.
POST /api/generate-event MUST reject a missing prompt with 400 and MUST return the five-field JSON draft for a valid prompt.
The endpoint MUST return a 500 with an error message when the provider call or JSON parsing fails.
The provider key MUST be read from the server environment only.
Generated values MUST fill the form without persisting an event.
The client MUST surface a request failure with a toast.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Provider credentials MUST NOT be exposed to the browser.
AI generation MUST remain optional; a failure MUST NOT prevent manual event creation.
The feature MUST pass ESLint, TypeScript checking, and SpecDrive governance validation.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The client disables Generate and the server returns 400.
The lazy client throws a clear error and the route returns 500.

edgeCases.description: The provider errors or returns an empty completion.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The route returns 500 with the provider message.
JSON.parse fails and the route returns 500.

edgeCases.description: The model returns an unknown category.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The value is written into the form as-is; the select may not match it.

edgeCases.description: The endpoint returns a non-2xx JSON error.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The client currently treats the body as generated data because response.ok is not checked.

risks.description: The route has no authentication or rate limiting, so it is publicly callable and can spend provider credits.
risks.mitigation: Require a session and apply a per-user rate limit before exposing the feature broadly.

risks.description: Model output is not validated against a schema before it is returned or applied.
risks.mitigation: Validate the response with Zod and reject unexpected categories or types.

risks.description: The client ignores the HTTP status, so error bodies can be applied as drafts.
risks.mitigation: Check response.ok and surface the error without calling onEventGenerated.

risks.description: The hard-coded model name and provider behaviour can change.
risks.mitigation: Move the model to configuration and monitor provider changes.
